Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. When superseding a decision or replacing code or content, delete the old thing outright. Never, on the agent's own initiative: keep legacy, old or superseded content even demoted or for reference; create backups; leave fallback paths; or leave tests and scripts in place. Any preservation of any kind requires the user's explicit approval first. This is a from-scratch thesis artefact, and legacy, fallbacks, backups and stale tests are bloat that pollutes both the codebase and the record; the user has flagged it repeatedly and treats it as a hard rule, not a preference. Replacing X with Y means removing X, not demoting it, commenting it out, or keeping a superseded-but-informative note; do not invent fallbacks for a chosen path; stale defaults pointing at the old choice are a defect to fix, not a fallback to keep; and if preservation genuinely seems warranted, ask first.
